simpleVersion: King Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya what his sons and the Pandavas did after gathering on the sacred battlefield of Kurukshetra.
explanation: King Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya to report what is happening on the holy plain of Kurukshetra. Both his own sons and the sons of Pandu have gathered there, ready for battle. He wants to know what they did once they assembled.

source.sanskrit:
धृतराष्ट्र उवाच

धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः।

मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत सञ्जय।।1.1।।
source.transliteration:
dhṛitarāśhtra uvācha
dharma-kṣhetre kuru-kṣhetre samavetā yuyutsavaḥ
māmakāḥ pāṇḍavāśhchaiva kimakurvata sañjaya
source.translation: Dhritarashtra said, "What did my people and the sons of Pandu do when they had assembled together, eager for battle, on the holy plain of Kurukshetra, O Sanjaya?"

simpleVersion: Sanjaya describes how King Duryodhana observed the organized Pandava army and went to talk to his teacher, Drona.
explanation: Sanjaya reports what is happening on the battlefield. King Duryodhana sees that the opposing Pandava army is fully prepared and arranged for battle. Seeing this, he walks over to speak with his teacher, Drona.

source.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच

दृष्ट्वा तु पाण्डवानीकं व्यूढं दुर्योधनस्तदा।

आचार्यमुपसङ्गम्य राजा वचनमब्रवीत्।।1.2।।
source.transliteration:
sañjaya uvācha
dṛiṣhṭvā tu pāṇḍavānīkaṁ vyūḍhaṁ duryodhanastadā
āchāryamupasaṅgamya rājā vachanamabravīt
source.translation: Sanjaya said: Having seen the army of the Pandavas drawn up in battle array, King Duryodhana approached his teacher, Drona, and spoke these words.

simpleVersion: Duryodhana points out the large Pandava army to his teacher, noting it was organized by his teacher's talented student.
explanation: In this verse, Duryodhana speaks to his teacher, Drona. He asks him to look at the massive army gathered by the Pandavas. He highlights that this army was arranged by the son of Drupada, who is Drona's own skilled student.

source.sanskrit:
पश्यैतां पाण्डुपुत्राणामाचार्य महतीं चमूम्।

व्यूढां द्रुपदपुत्रेण तव शिष्येण धीमता।।1.3।।
source.transliteration:
paśhyaitāṁ pāṇḍu-putrāṇām āchārya mahatīṁ chamūm
vyūḍhāṁ drupada-putreṇa tava śhiṣhyeṇa dhīmatā
source.translation: Behold, O Teacher! This mighty army of the sons of Pandu, arrayed by the son of Drupada, thy wise disciple.

simpleVersion: This verse lists great archers and heroic warriors in the army who are as powerful in battle as Bhima and Arjuna.
explanation: This verse names several powerful heroes and archers present on the battlefield. It highlights skilled warriors like Yuyudhana, Virata, and Drupada, comparing their strength in battle to famous fighters like Bhima and Arjuna.

source.sanskrit:
अत्र शूरा महेष्वासा भीमार्जुनसमा युधि।

युयुधानो विराटश्च द्रुपदश्च महारथः।।1.4।।
source.transliteration:
atra śhūrā maheṣhvāsā bhīmārjuna-samā yudhi
yuyudhāno virāṭaśhcha drupadaśhcha mahā-rathaḥ
source.translation: Here are heroes, mighty archers, equal in battle to Bhima and Arjuna, Yuyudhana (Satyaki), Virata, and Drupada—all mighty warriors.

simpleVersion: This verse names several heroic kings and warriors present on the battlefield, describing them as the best of men.
explanation: This verse lists key warriors standing on the battlefield. It names Dhrishtaketu, Chekitana, the powerful king of Kasi, Purujit, Kuntibhoja, and Saibya. These individuals are praised as outstanding and brave leaders among men.

source.sanskrit:
धृष्टकेतुश्चेकितानः काशिराजश्च वीर्यवान्।

पुरुजित्कुन्तिभोजश्च शैब्यश्च नरपुङ्गवः।।1.5।।
source.transliteration:
dhṛiṣhṭaketuśhchekitānaḥ kāśhirājaśhcha vīryavān
purujit kuntibhojaśhcha śhaibyaśhcha nara-puṅgavaḥ
yudhāmanyuśhcha vikrānta uttamaujāśhcha vīryavān
source.translation: Dhrishtaketu, Chekitana, the valiant king of Kasi, Purujit, Kuntibhoja, and Saibya—the best of men.

simpleVersion: This verse lists powerful warriors in the army, including Yudhamanyu, Uttamaujas, Abhimanyu, and the sons of Draupadi, calling them all great heroes.
explanation: Duryodhana continues naming the key fighters on the opposing side. He highlights strong warriors like Yudhamanyu, brave Uttamaujas, Abhimanyu, and Draupadi’s sons. He recognizes that all of them are elite warriors.

source.sanskrit:
युधामन्युश्च विक्रान्त उत्तमौजाश्च वीर्यवान्।

सौभद्रो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्व एव महारथाः।।1.6।।
source.translation: The strong Yudhamanyu and the brave Uttamaujas, the son of Subhadra (Abhimanyu, the son of Subhadra and Arjuna), and the sons of Draupadi, all of them great charioteers (great heroes)."

simpleVersion: Duryodhana speaks to his teacher and offers to list the key commanders leading their army.
explanation: Duryodhana addresses his teacher, calling him the best among the twice-born. He wants to point out the most distinguished leaders commanding their army so his teacher is fully informed.

source.sanskrit:
अस्माकं तु विशिष्टा ये तान्निबोध द्विजोत्तम।

नायका मम सैन्यस्य संज्ञार्थं तान्ब्रवीमि ते।।1.7।।
source.transliteration:
asmākaṁ tu viśhiṣhṭā ye tānnibodha dwijottama
nāyakā mama sainyasya sanjñārthaṁ tānbravīmi te
source.translation: Know also, O best among the twice-born! the names of those who are the most distinguished amongst ourselves, the leaders of my army; these I name to you for your information.

simpleVersion: This verse names major victorious warriors—including Bhishma, Karna, Kripa, Asvatthama, Vikarna, and Bhurisrava—who are fully prepared for battle.
explanation: In this verse, specific powerful military leaders ready for combat are named. These fighters include Bhishma, Karna, Kripa, Asvatthama, Vikarna, and Bhurisrava. They are all described as victorious warriors who are assembled and prepared to fight.

source.sanskrit:
भवान्भीष्मश्च कर्णश्च कृपश्च समितिञ्जयः।

अश्वत्थामा विकर्णश्च सौमदत्तिस्तथैव च।।1.8।।
source.transliteration:
bhavānbhīṣhmaśhcha karṇaśhcha kṛipaśhcha samitiñjayaḥ
aśhvatthāmā vikarṇaśhcha saumadattis tathaiva cha
source.translation: "Thou thyself, Bhishma, Karna, Kripa, the victorious in war, Asvatthama, Vikarna, and Bhurisrava, the son of Somadatta—all these are ready for battle."

simpleVersion: Duryodhana points out that many other skilled heroes, armed with various weapons, are ready to lay down their lives for him.
explanation: Duryodhana is describing the rest of his army to Drona. He points out that there are many brave warriors who are highly trained in battle and equipped with many types of weapons. Crucially, these fighters are willing to risk and give up their lives for his cause.

source.sanskrit:
अन्ये च बहवः शूरा मदर्थे त्यक्तजीविताः।

नानाशस्त्रप्रहरणाः सर्वे युद्धविशारदाः।।1.9।।
source.transliteration:
anye cha bahavaḥ śhūrā madarthe tyaktajīvitāḥ
nānā-śhastra-praharaṇāḥ sarve yuddha-viśhāradāḥ
source.translation: And also many other heroes, ready to give up their lives for my sake, armed with various weapons and missiles, all well-skilled in battle.

simpleVersion: Duryodhana states that his army, protected by Bhishma, is insufficient, while the opposing army, led by Bhima, is sufficient.
explanation: In this verse, Duryodhana compares the strength of the two opposing forces. He assesses his own army, commanded by Bhishma, as inadequate. In contrast, he considers the enemy army, guarded by Bhima, to be fully sufficient.

source.sanskrit:
अपर्याप्तं तदस्माकं बलं भीष्माभिरक्षितम्।

पर्याप्तं त्विदमेतेषां बलं भीमाभिरक्षितम्।।1.10।।
source.transliteration:
aparyāptaṁ tadasmākaṁ balaṁ bhīṣhmābhirakṣhitam
paryāptaṁ tvidameteṣhāṁ balaṁ bhīmābhirakṣhitam
source.translation: Our army, marshalled by Bhishma, is insufficient, whereas theirs, marshalled by Bhima, is sufficient.
